correctness.rationale: Setting t=log|x|/log(lambda) reduces the invariance equation to P(t+1)=(I+N)P(t)+lambda^(-k)v. Pascal gives P_*(t)=lambda^(-k) sum_{r=1}^m binom(t,r) N^(r-1)v; all homogeneous solutions on bounded fundamental intervals grow at most t^(m-1) under J^n. Thus first-coordinate coefficient is v_m/(lambda^k m!(log lambda)^m). A C^(k-1,1) graph has vanishing derivatives through k-1 and hence O(x^k), impossible for v_m!=0. When v_m=0, v is in ran N and polynomial graph ax^k exists. Orbit formula yields normalized n^m limit. Endpoint m=1 and both sign half-lines included.
residual_risks: Universal asymptotic requires bounded fundamental-interval data and continuity on each punctured side; only canonical constructed graph is guaranteed C^(k-1,alpha).
